analysis.title: Market volatility reinforces case for portfolio resilience
key_insights: US equities fell again on Thursday on AI-trade concerns and a more hawkish rate backdrop. The S&P 500 closed down 2% and the Nasdaq Composite down 2.3%. All major S&P 500 sectors fell and decliners substantially outnumbered advancers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq.

Minutes from the Fed's October meeting indicated nearly all policymakers expected further tightening to be necessary if the US economy evolves as anticipated. Markets priced a near certainty of a 25bp hike in December.

Gold fell to a 14-month low of around USD 3,654 an ounce on higher rate expectations and dollar strength. US 2-year and 10-year yields fell 4bps and 2bps respectively, and the dollar rose modestly against most major currencies.

Hunterbrook's short-sell report on AMD (-7.7%) cited fears that its China business may be hit by stricter US chip restrictions. NVIDIA (-3.3%) extended recent losses despite an upbeat revenue forecast earlier in the week.

UBS does not think the economic expansion, earnings cycle or structural AI investment story has broken. The 2027 base case is near-trend growth, rising profits, more AI investment and moderating inflation later in the year.

UBS recently downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral, citing elevated expectations, high index concentration and a wider range of AI outcomes. The AI debate is shifting from whether investment continues to whether it can generate sufficient revenue and shareholder returns.

Cumulative US tech AI infrastructure investment could approach USD 5tr by end-2028. UBS estimates AI model and application revenues must reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate return. Competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models threaten returns.
UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 but not a prolonged tightening cycle. Higher rates should weigh on consumer demand, and base effects should moderate underlying inflation.

Equity positioning: about 15% S&P 500 earnings growth expected in 2027. The top 10 companies are 39% of the index. The Eurozone is the preferred region (15% earnings growth forecast, lower valuation than the US). UBS favors industrials and health care, and equal-weight US strategies to reduce tech concentration.

Within US tech, UBS favors financially strong hyperscalers with visible AI monetization and select leaders in compute, foundry, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software. It is cautious on leveraged capacity providers, lower-quality suppliers and companies dependent on persistent bottlenecks or distant cash flows.

Fixed income: UBS favors intermediate duration (2 to 10 years). Best return opportunity is in EM and high yield bonds. EM sovereign and corporate bonds yield roughly 7.1% and 7.0%, and US high yield about 8.3%.

UBS advises using volatility via structured strategies that can limit losses, generate income or allow measured participation. Higher implied volatility raises their appeal, but capital loss, issuer, liquidity and opportunity-cost risks require diversification and careful sizing.

The Australian dollar erased all its 2026 gains after October unemployment rose to a five-year high of 4.9% (est 4.7%) with 43,500 jobs lost (forecast +25,000). AUDUSD closed at 0.6656, an eighth straight daily decline. The RBA has hiked five times this year to 4.85%, and its latest vote was split 6-3.

UBS downgraded the Australian dollar to Unattractive, since the property downturn and rising unemployment raise the risk that the RBA is among the first major central banks to cut in 2027. Further AUDUSD declines are possible near term. UBS expects USD strength to fade from Q2 2027 and favors the British pound and select EM currencies.

Three-month LME copper fell over 7% in two days to its lowest since April on AI-growth concerns, Fed tightening and tariff skepticism. UBS attributes this to weaker sentiment and rising exchange inventories, not weaker fundamentals, and stays constructive with a USD 15,500/mt forecast by mid-2027.

US managed care shares sold off after CMS proposed tighter Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment oversight. The S&P 500 Managed Health Care Index fell around 14% since Monday's close. CMS estimates savings of almost USD 90bn over 10 years. UBS expects negligible earnings effects over the next two years because similar audit efforts have faced legal challenges.
